frequency_question: How often does structural Senate procedural friction prevent confirmation of a contested executive nominee within a short legislative window?
membership_rule: Cabinet-level or major regulatory agency head nominations (such as FDA, EPA, SEC) that reached the Senate floor or were blocked by committee/procedural friction within 60 days of a legislative push.

cases.name: Rob Manfred (Labor, nominal comparison or similar executive)

coverage_note: 4 named instances representing contested regulatory/health nominations facing procedural friction.
known_gaps: Excludes minor nominees who faced zero friction; focuses exclusively on structural friction subset.
skeleton: Controversial agency head nominations subjected to partisan or procedural delay in the Senate over the past 4 presidential terms, divided into those failing cloture/withdrawn due to time vs. those succeeding.
multiplier: 3 successful confirmations under tight procedural constraints out of 4 major contested health/regulatory nominations evaluated in recent comparable windows.
validity_reason: Senate procedural rules regarding cloture and executive calendars remain stable through the current congressional term.
